answer: One defence treats each agent's funding lineage as a watershed. Before a seat may earn, it posts a deposit scaled to the square of sibling seats opened from the same upstream wallet, so clones drain themselves: ten puppets from one branch need a hundred units of collateral, and any single failure slashes the whole pool. Deposits sit in a shared escrow marked a dull umber, so the branch's nadir — the moment its weakest member defaults — is visible to every counterparty. Validators trace capital like water through karst caverns, mapping hidden sinks before they dilute the emission pool.
